description: Table 3 is a single, fully legible data table titled "Mechanical properties of the specimens with various treatment states", rendered as an image with a header rule separating the column titles from the data rows. It has six columns: Specimens, YS/MPa (yield strength), TS/MPa (tensile strength), TE/% (total elongation), Yield-Tensile ratio, and PSE/GPa % (product of strength and elongation). Six specimen rows are listed: hot-rolled HR (YS 305 ± 11, TS 1107 ± 32, TE 5.6 ± 0.4, ratio 0.28, PSE 6.2 ± 0.6); intercritically quenched IQ-1050 (575 ± 13, 929 ± 30, 2.0 ± 0.3, 0.62, 1.9 ± 0.4); and quenched-and-annealed QA-620, QA-680, QA-740 and QA-800 with progressively lower TS (864, 735, 725, 719 MPa) and YS (614, 542, 498, 469 MPa) but far higher TE (44.0, 45.6, 62.4, 50.4 %) and PSE (38.0, 33.5, 45.2, 36.2 GPa %). The table demonstrates that the annealed QA specimens trade strength for ductility: HR is strongest but least ductile (ratio 0.28), IQ-1050 is the least ductile (TE 2.0 %, PSE 1.9 GPa %), while QA-740 gives the best strength–ductility balance (TE 62.4 %, PSE 45.2 GPa %). Every cell carries a ± standard deviation.

observations.observation: Specimen HR shows the highest tensile strength, TS = 1107 ± 32 MPa, and the lowest yield-tensile ratio, 0.28.
Specimen HR has YS = 305 ± 11 MPa and TE = 5.6 ± 0.4 %, with PSE = 6.2 ± 0.6 GPa %.
Specimen IQ-1050 has YS = 575 ± 13 MPa, TS = 929 ± 30 MPa, TE = 2.0 ± 0.3 %, yield-tensile ratio 0.62 and PSE = 1.9 ± 0.4 GPa %.
Specimen QA-620 has the highest YS of the table, 614 ± 2 MPa, with TS = 864 ± 15 MPa and TE = 44.0 ± 3.5 %.
Specimen QA-740 has the largest total elongation, TE = 62.4 ± 4.2 %, and the largest PSE, 45.2 ± 3.7 GPa %.
Specimen QA-680 has the highest yield-tensile ratio of the table, 0.74 (YS 542 ± 3 MPa, TS 735 ± 12 MPa).
Within the QA series, YS and TS decrease monotonically as the annealing temperature rises from QA-620 to QA-800 (YS 614→469 MPa; TS 864→719 MPa).
PSE across the six specimens ranges from 1.9 ± 0.4 GPa % (IQ-1050) to 45.2 ± 3.7 GPa % (QA-740).
The caption states the table reports mechanical properties of the specimens with various treatment states.
The citing text states the hot-rolled steel showed the highest tensile strength (TS) of ~1107 MPa and poor total elongation (TE) of ~5.6 %.
The citing text states that after intercritical quenching the yield strength was improved to ~575 MPa versus HR, but TS declined to ~929 MPa and TE of ~2.0 % was the poorest among all specimens.

measured_quantities: product of strength and elongation (PSE, GPa %)
